- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.
- After a sharp spike in true price, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model underestimates price; add 3–8% to forecast mean to compensate for supply constraint.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model is rising, cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak to avoid false recovery signals.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., >10% drop from peak), model should be adjusted downward by 5–10% in next 10–15 days.
- If recent events show high bearish sentiment + supply net negative, model should be adjusted downward by 3–7% to reflect policy/supply pressure.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and model is flat, introduce 1–3% upward drift to capture latent bullish sentiment.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome for 3+ days, increase forecast slope by 1–3% to reflect lagged market reaction.
